wrong_one_examples.text: 代词错误：“move it to a new spot”应为“move them to a new spot”。要根据位置使用主格或宾格（I／me、he／him）；反身代词（himself）只有在同一分句中有先行词时才能用；指人用 who 而不是 which；关系从句中不要再加多余的代词；代词要与所指对象的数一致（指几个东西用 them，指一个用 it）。
wrong_one_examples.J1_note: Invents many unrelated pronoun rules; the gold error is only one pronoun.

wrong_one_examples.text: Meaning reversed: here your sentence says the opposite of the original — the reference has “看起来非常开心”. A small change such as a dropped “not”, an opposite word or a reversed direction can flip the meaning, so this is a serious error even when the sentence looks almost right.

wrong_one_examples.text: Adverbs like '都' must precede the verb. Placing it after the subject but before the object breaks the standard S-Adv-V-O structure in Chinese.
wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Claims S-Adv-V-O structure, but claims 都 is placed before object, which is false.

wrong_one_examples.text: In Japanese, the adverb "とても" (very) must come before the i-adjective "シンプルな" (simple) to modify it. Placing them in reverse order breaks the grammatical structure needed to describe the robot arm.
wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Incorrectly calls シンプルな an i-adjective instead of a na-adjective.

wrong_one_examples.text: The stem is right but the ending is built incorrectly for its conjugation class (godan, ichidan, irregular; い- or な-adjective).

wrong_one_examples.text: "見つけれる" is grammatically incorrect because "見つける" is a godan verb, which requires the potential form "見つけられる" to express ability. Using "見つけれる" changes the structure incorrectly and sounds unnatural compared to the standard potential form.
wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Falsely claims 見つける is a godan verb.

wrong_one_examples.text: 「見つけれる」mixes two verb classes: 見つける is an ichidan (ru-)verb, so its potential form keeps the full られ pattern. Dropping ら is fine, but swapping in れ for ら is not.
wrong_one_examples.J1_note: Calls 見つける ichidan (true) but says dropping ら is fine, which the gold error contradicts.
wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Misexplains ra-nuki kotoba mechanism.

wrong_one_examples.text: You wrote 見つけれる. Think about how the potential form of 見つける is built — which helper ending goes after the stem for an ichidan verb? Check that your form matches the pattern you used elsewhere in the sentence.
wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Leaked the answer by suggesting checking the pattern used elsewhere (調整できるように).

wrong_one_examples.text: For this potential form, 見つける is an ichidan verb, so add られる to its stem. The ら-dropping option applies to 見れる, but not to 見つけれる.

wrong_one_examples.J2_note: Falsely claims 見れる is ra-nuki but 見つけれる is not.
